answer: One Sybil defense in an AI-agent economy is stake-weighted identity: an agent locks collateral for voting power, and influence equals capital bonded, not account count. Splitting one purse into a thousand fakes adds no weight, since the attacker must post the same total stake across every shell; each new identity raises cost, not power. Caught double-voting, his bond is slashed and burned. A jade coin can ripple into many reflections yet stay one saffron mass: the split is cosmetic. A majority attack costs as much capital as all honest agents combined, making forgery irrational.
